channel.title: Michigan Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Michigan Lawyers Weekly (milawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Delaware dog custody battle wraps up with unexpected auction
item.description: Delaware's Chancery Court ended a lengthy custody battle over a goldendoodle named Tucker by ordering a sealed bid auction between the estranged owners.

item.title: Supreme Court asked to rule on pot use, regulation
item.description: The Michigan Supreme Court will soon decide whether prohibiting marijuana use while on probation is legal.

item.title: Court denies injunction to enforce noncompete
item.description: An employer was not entitled to a preliminary injunction to enforce a noncompete against a former employee where the agreement contained overly broad restrictions.

item.title: Employment – Discrimination
item.description: Where plaintiffs have brought a class action alleging racial discrimination and related claims connected to their prior employment as security personnel at the Renaissance Center in Detroit, the defendants’ motion to require the plaintiffs to submit a more definite statement of their claims should be denied because the complaint provides the defendants with sufficient notice of the claims against them.

item.title: Construction truck rear-ends vehicle in freeway collision
item.description: This case arose from a freeway collision involving a passenger vehicle and a commercial construction truck. item.title: Negligence – Comparative fault – Suicide
item.description: Where a negligence suit was brought following the suicide of a 15-year-old resident at the Calumet Center, the trial court erred by granting summary disposition in plaintiffs’ favor regarding comparative fault.

item.title: Municipal – Land transfer agreement
item.description: Where a complaint was filed after the Ccity of Marshall entered into a land transfer agreement with Marshall Township, the trial court did not err when it dismissed the plaintiff’s claim in Count IV that Ordinance 2023-08 violated a “Master 425 Agreement.”

item.title: Insurance – Limitations period – Appraisal
item.description: Where a defendant insurer was awarded summary disposition in a suit over damage to a home, that judgment must be reversed in part, as an issue exists regarding whether the policy’s limitations period provision bars the plaintiffs’ claims.

item.title: Employment – Whistleblower
item.description: Where a plaintiff alleged retaliation under the Whistleblower Protection Act, a grant of summary disposition in favor of the defendants should be affirmed because the plaintiff failed to offer any evidence demonstrating pretext.

item.title: Employment – Limitations period – Integration clause
item.description: Where a defendant employer moved for summary judgment based on a six-month limitations period in the plaintiff’s job application, it was proper to deny that motion because the parties’ employment agreement, which contains an integration clause, does not contain a shortened limitations period.

item.title: Plaintiff sustains serious neurologic impairment after highway ramp crash
item.description: A schoolteacher sustained serious neurologic impairment as a result of the defendants’ vehicle allegedly attempting to erratically change lanes on a highway ramp.

item.title: Jurisdiction lacking over petition to confirm arbitration award
item.description: A petition in U.S. District Court to confirm an arbitration award has been dismissed for lack of subject matter jurisdiction.

item.title: ‘Abscondment’ doesn’t toll term of supervised release, SCOTUS rules
item.description: U.S. Supreme Court rules absconding does not extend supervised release, resolving a circuit split in Rico v. United States.

item.title: U.S. exempts Gulf of Mexico drillers from protecting endangered species
item.description: The endangered species committee exempted Gulf of Mexico oil and gas drillers from the Endangered Species Act, citing national security concerns.

item.title: Use of outdated mortality data barred by ERISA
item.description: A divided 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals panel ruled that pension plans cannot use unreasonably outdated mortality data under ERISA's actuarial equivalence requirement.
